title: Boiled pasta (any shape)
summary: Perfect al dente pasta. Remy asks which shape you're boiling and sets the right timer.
source: Written for REMY by Claude, timers from cook-times.json (pasta_dried_minutes_al_dente). Waiting for Matthew's review.
notes: REMY: before starting the timer, ASK which pasta shape it is and use step 3's timer_by_shape (from cook-times.json). Say the timer out loud and that the packet time wins: 'Penne, 11 minutes. Shout if your packet says different.' If the shape isn't listed, ask for the packet time and use that. Never guess.
ingredients: 200g dried pasta, any shape (about 100g per person)
Optional: butter, olive oil or your sauce to serve

steps.instruction: Tell Remy which pasta you're boiling (penne, fusilli, spaghetti…) and check the cooking time on the packet.
steps.ask: Which pasta shape are you boiling? And what time does the packet say?
looks_right: the pasta packet held up to the camera
looks_wrong: no packet in view and no shape given (ask again)
steps.done_when: Remy knows the shape (and the packet time if there is one).

steps.instruction: Fill a large pot with about 2 litres of water, cover it and bring it to a big rolling boil on high. Then add the salt.
looks_right: big bubbles breaking the surface all over
looks_wrong: only tiny bubbles on the bottom (not boiling yet)
a small pot with too little water (the pasta will stick)
steps.done_when: The water is at a big rolling boil and salted.

steps.instruction: Tip in the pasta and stir straight away so it doesn't stick. Remy starts the timer for your shape as soon as it's in.
looks_right: pasta moving freely in the bubbling water
spaghetti softened and pushed under the water
looks_wrong: pasta clumped together or stuck to the bottom
foam about to boil over (turn the heat down a little)
steps.done_when: The pasta is in, stirred, and the timer for that shape is running.

steps.instruction: Stir every couple of minutes, especially in the first two, and keep it at a lively boil.
looks_wrong: foam rising to the rim (heat down a notch)
boil dropped to a simmer (heat up)
steps.done_when: The timer reaches its check point.

steps.instruction: When the timer says check, taste a piece. Al dente means tender with a little bite in the middle. Scoop out a mug of pasta water, then drain.
looks_right: the bite shows no chalky white core
steps.done_when: The pasta passes the bite test and is drained, with a mug of water saved. Ask the cook to bite a piece or hold one up to the camera.

steps.instruction: Toss it straight away with butter, olive oil or your sauce, adding a splash of pasta water if it looks dry. Serve hot.
looks_wrong: drained pasta left sitting in the colander (it sticks together)
